Data

ACS-5
```{r}
my_vars <- c(
  tot_pop = "B01003_001",
  pop_povstat = "B17001A_002",
  medhhinc = "B25119_001",
  white = "C02003_003",
  black = "C02003_004",
  asian = "C02003_006",
  hispanic = "B03001_003",
  hu_ownocc = "B25003_002",
  divorced_m = "B12001_010",  # Male: Now divorced
  divorced_f = "B12001_019",  # Female: Now divorced
  tot_hu = "B25001_001"
)

census_data <- get_acs(
  geography = "county",
  variables = my_vars,
  year = 2019,
  survey = "acs5",
  geometry = TRUE,
  cache_table = TRUE
) %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, variable, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = variable,
    values_from = estimate
  )

census_data <- census_data %>%
  mutate(divorced = divorced_m + divorced_f)
```

Prisons (ICPSR)
```{r}
#US Prisons (from ICPSR)
#The raw dataset contains 6,468 prison facilities with geographic boundaries.
#Two filters are applied: (1) only facilities with STATUS "OPEN" or "CLOSED" are
#retained, dropping ambiguous or unknown statuses; (2) TYPE "COUNTY" is excluded,
#removing local jails which were not sited as economic development tools and do not
#fit the theoretical framework of the study. The cleaned dataset is then collapsed
#to the county level using COUNTYFIPS, producing counts and capacity/population
#totals broken out by status (open, closed, and combined).

prisons_icpsr <- st_read("data/prison-boundaries-1-geojson.geojson")

#names(prisons_icpsr)

prisons_clean <- prisons_icpsr %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(
    STATUS %in% c("OPEN", "CLOSED"),
    TYPE != "COUNTY"
  )

prisons_by_county <- prisons_clean %>%
  group_by(COUNTYFIPS) %>%
  summarise(
    num_prisons        = n(),
    num_open           = sum(STATUS == "OPEN"),
    num_closed         = sum(STATUS == "CLOSED"),
    capacity_total     = sum(CAPACITY, na.rm = TRUE),
    capacity_open      = sum(CAPACITY[STATUS == "OPEN"],   na.rm = TRUE),
    capacity_closed    = sum(CAPACITY[STATUS == "CLOSED"], na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_total          = sum(POPULATION, na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_open           = sum(POPULATION[STATUS == "OPEN"],   na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_closed         = sum(POPULATION[STATUS == "CLOSED"], na.rm = TRUE)
  )


```

Death counts
```{r}
#death counts and death rates for drug overdose, suicide, homicide and firearm injuries by county of residence

#The raw dataset contains county-level death counts and rates for drug overdose,
#firearm injuries, homicide, and suicide across multiple years. The data is filtered
#to 2019 and restricted to three Intent categories relevant to the distress index:
#Drug_OD, All_Suicide, and All_Homicide. Firearm-specific subcategories (FA_Suicide,
#FA_Homicide, FA_Deaths) are dropped to avoid double-counting, as they are subsets
#of the all-cause homicide and suicide totals. Rate is coerced to numeric, and the
#dataset is pivoted to wide format so each county appears as a single row with
#separate rate columns for each outcome. Small cell counts (1-9 deaths) reported
#as ranges by the CDC are handled by using the pre-computed Rate column directly,
#bypassing the suppression issue in the Count column entirely.


injury_overdose_violence <- read_csv("data/injury_overdose_violence.csv")


#2019
injury_overdose_violence_2019 <- injury_overdose_violence %>%
  filter(Period == "2019") %>%                        # fix: string not numeric
  filter(Intent %in% c("Drug_OD", "All_Suicide",     # only what you need
                        "All_Homicide")) %>%
  mutate(Rate = as.numeric(Rate)) %>%                 # ensure numeric
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols    = c(GEOID, NAME, ST_GEOID, ST_NAME),
    names_from  = Intent,
    values_from = c(Rate),
    names_glue  = "{Intent}_rate"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    overdose_rate = Drug_OD_rate,
    suicide_rate  = All_Suicide_rate,
    homicide_rate = All_Homicide_rate
  )


```

Unemployment (BLS)
```{r}
#BLS (unemployment rate)

# The raw BLS county unemployment file for 2019 is structured with the title row
# as the first row and the actual column headers as the second row, a common BLS
# formatting issue. The column names are manually assigned via set_names(), and the
# spurious header row is dropped with slice(-1). Trailing footnote rows are removed
# by filtering out blank state FIPS values. State and county FIPS codes, stored in
# separate columns in the raw file, are padded to 2 and 3 digits respectively and
# concatenated into a single 5-digit GEOID to match the join key used across all
# other datasets. All numeric columns are coerced from character, and the dataset
# is reduced to the GEOID, county name, and core labor force variables.

unemployment_2019 <- read_excel("data/unemployment19.xlsx")

unemployment_2019_clean <- unemployment_2019 %>%
  set_names(c("laus_code", "state_fips", "county_fips", 
              "county_name", "year", "labor_force", 
              "employed", "unemployed", "unemp_rate")) %>%
  slice(-1) %>%                                        
  filter(!is.na(state_fips), state_fips != "") %>%     
  mutate(
    GEOID     = paste0(
                  str_pad(state_fips,  2, pad = "0"),
                  str_pad(county_fips, 3, pad = "0")
                ),
    unemp_rate = as.numeric(unemp_rate),
    labor_force = as.numeric(labor_force),
    employed    = as.numeric(employed),
    unemployed  = as.numeric(unemployed)
  ) %>%
  select(GEOID, county_name, labor_force, employed, unemployed, unemp_rate)
```

Urban vs. Rural counties (USDA)
```{r}
#Urban vs. Rural counties (from USDA)
#2023
#rural_2023 <- read_csv("data/rural_urban_codes2023.csv") #1-3:urban, 4-9:rural

#rural_wide <- rural_2023 %>%

#  ) %>%

#    Population_2020 = as.numeric(Population_2020),
#    RUCC_2023 = as.numeric(RUCC_2023)
#  )



#2013
# The 2013 Rural-Urban Continuum Codes (RUCC) from the USDA are already in wide
# format with one row per county. The only cleaning needed is renaming FIPS to GEOID
# for consistency with the join key used across all other datasets, and creating a
# binary rural indicator following the standard USDA convention where codes 1-3
# denote metro (urban) counties and codes 4-9 denote nonmetro (rural) counties.
# The 2013 vintage is used rather than 2023 because it predates the 2019 outcome
# year, which is the methodologically appropriate choice.

rural_2013 <- read_excel("data/rural_urban_codes2013.xls")

rural_2013_clean <- rural_2013 %>%
  rename(GEOID = FIPS) %>%
  mutate(rural = as.integer(RUCC_2013 >= 4)) %>%
  select(GEOID, State, County_Name, Population_2010, RUCC_2013, rural, Description)
```

Life Expectancy (from CDC, 2010-2015)

```{r}
# Life expectancy data comes from the USALEEP project (2010-2015), the most
# comprehensive source of county-level life expectancy available for the contiguous
# US. The raw file is at the census tract level (73,121 tracts), so it must be
# aggregated to the county level. Rather than a simple mean, a population-weighted
# mean is computed so that more populous tracts contribute proportionally more to
# the county estimate, which better reflects the lived experience of the average
# county resident. Tract-level population denominators are pulled from the 2011-2015
# ACS 5-year estimates (variable B01003_001) via tidycensus, looping over all 51
# state-level calls required by the API. A county FIPS crosswalk is constructed from
# the built-in fips_codes dataframe in tidycensus and joined to the life expectancy
# file on county name. Tract numbers in the USALEEP file (e.g. "0201.00") are
# reformatted into standard 11-digit Census GEOIDs by removing the decimal point,
# padding to 6 digits, and prepending the 5-digit county FIPS code. The 2010-2015
# vintage is used as it is the only nationally comprehensive county-level life
# expectancy dataset available; this measurement lag relative to the 2019 outcome
# year is acknowledged as a limitation.

life_expectancy <- read_csv("data/life_expectancy_2010-2015.csv")
all_states <- unique(fips_codes$state)[1:51]
tract_pop <- map_dfr(all_states, function(s) {
  get_acs(
    geography = "tract",
    variables = c(tract_pop = "B01003_001"),
    state     = s,
    year      = 2015,
    survey    = "acs5",
    geometry  = FALSE
  )
}) %>%
  select(GEOID, tract_pop = estimate)

fips_xwalk <- fips_codes %>%
  mutate(
    county_full = paste0(county, ", ", state),
    county_fips = paste0(state_code, county_code)
  ) %>%
  select(county_full, county_fips)

life_expectancy_clean <- life_expectancy %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  filter(county != "(blank)", !is.na(census_tract_number)) %>%
  left_join(fips_xwalk, by = c("county" = "county_full")) %>%
  mutate(
    tract_clean = str_remove(census_tract_number, "\\.") %>%
                  str_pad(6, pad = "0"),
    GEOID = paste0(county_fips, tract_clean)
  )

life_expectancy_county <- life_expectancy_clean %>%
  left_join(tract_pop, by = "GEOID") %>%
  group_by(county_fips, state, county) %>%
  summarise(
    life_exp_weighted = weighted.mean(life_expectancy,
                                      w     = tract_pop,
                                      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_tracts = n()
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(GEOID = county_fips)
```


Occupation - Correctional Institution
```{r}
occupation <- read_csv("data/occupation_correctional_institution.csv")

# QCEW correctional employment (NAICS 92214), 2019
# Due to disclosure suppression affecting 88% of county-level records,
# employment is coded as a three-category variable rather than a continuous measure.

occupation_clean <- occupation %>%
  filter(agglvl_code == 77) %>%
  group_by(area_fips) %>%
  summarise(
    correctional_emplvl = sum(annual_avg_emplvl, na.rm = TRUE),
    any_suppressed      = any(disclosure_code == "N"),
    any_reported        = any(is.na(disclosure_code) & annual_avg_emplvl > 0)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    corr_employ_cat = case_when(
      any_reported   ~ "reported",
      any_suppressed ~ "suppressed",
      TRUE           ~ "none"
    )
  ) %>%
  rename(GEOID = area_fips)

master <- master %>%
  left_join(occupation_clean, by = "GEOID") %>%
  mutate(
    corr_employ_cat = replace_na(corr_employ_cat, "none"),
    correctional_emplvl = replace_na(correctional_emplvl, 0)
  )
```

```{r}
# fix -999 sentinel values in prisons before joining
prisons_by_county <- prisons_by_county %>%
  rename(GEOID = COUNTYFIPS) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~na_if(., -999L)))

# master join
master <- census_data %>%
  left_join(prisons_by_county,             by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(injury_overdose_violence_2019, by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(unemployment_2019_clean,       by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(rural_2013_clean,              by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(life_expectancy_county,        by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(occupation_clean,              by = "GEOID") %>%
  mutate(
    corr_employ_cat     = replace_na(corr_employ_cat, "none"),
    correctional_emplvl = replace_na(correctional_emplvl, 0)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !str_starts(GEOID, "02"),  # drop Alaska
    !str_starts(GEOID, "15")   # drop Hawaii
  )

master <- master %>%
  filter(str_length(GEOID) == 5,           # ensure proper county FIPS
         str_starts(GEOID, "0[1-9]") |     # states 01-09
         str_starts(GEOID, "[1-4][0-9]") | # states 10-49
         str_starts(GEOID, "5[0-6]"))       # states 50-56 (excl 57+)
```

```{r}
master_clean <- master %>%
  # fix -999 sentinel values across all numeric columns
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~na_if(., -999))) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~na_if(., -2997))) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~na_if(., -3996))) %>%
  # fix NaN in life expectancy
  mutate(life_exp_weighted = ifelse(is.nan(life_exp_weighted), 
                                    NA, life_exp_weighted)) %>%
  # drop redundant and unnecessary columns
  select(
    GEOID,
    name          = NAME.x,
    geometry,
    # ACS variables
    tot_pop, white, black, asian, hispanic,
    medhhinc, hu_ownocc, tot_hu,
    pop_povstat, divorced,
    # prison variables
    num_prisons, num_open, num_closed,
    capacity_total, capacity_open, capacity_closed,
    # outcome variables
    overdose_rate, suicide_rate, homicide_rate,
    # controls
    unemp_rate, RUCC_2013, rural,
    # life expectancy
    life_exp_weighted,
    # correctional employment
    corr_employ_cat, correctional_emplvl
  )
```

```{r}
master_clean <- master_clean %>%
  # replace NA with 0 for prison count variables
  # (NA means no prison in county, which is genuinely 0)
  mutate(
    num_prisons  = replace_na(num_prisons, 0),
    num_open     = replace_na(num_open, 0),
    num_closed   = replace_na(num_closed, 0)
  ) %>%
  # binary prison presence indicator
  mutate(
    prison_present = as.integer(num_open > 0)
  ) %>%
  # race/ethnicity as share of total population
  mutate(
    pct_white    = white    / tot_pop,
    pct_black    = black    / tot_pop,
    pct_asian    = asian    / tot_pop,
    pct_hispanic = hispanic / tot_pop
  ) %>%
  # other proportions
  mutate(
    pct_poverty     = pop_povstat / tot_pop,
    homeown_rate    = hu_ownocc   / tot_hu,
    divorce_rate    = divorced    / tot_pop
  ) %>%
  # population density would need area — do you have that?
  # log transform population for controls (highly skewed)
  mutate(
    log_pop      = log(tot_pop),
    log_medhhinc = log(medhhinc)
  )
```

```{r}
#nys domestic violence data (2012-2024)

#2024
nys_violence_2024_raw <- read_excel("data/nys_violence_2024.xlsx")

nys_violence_2024 <- nys_violence_2024_raw %>%
  rename(
    county = 1,
    offense_type = 2,
    female_intimate_partner = 3,
    male_intimate_partner = 4,
    total_intimate_partner = 5,
    other_family_victim = 6,
    total_all_victims = 7
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(female_intimate_partner:total_all_victims), as.numeric))

nys_violence_2024 <- nys_violence_2024 %>%
  fill(county)  

nys_violence_2024 <- nys_violence_2024 %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(female_intimate_partner, male_intimate_partner, other_family_victim),
    names_to = "victim_type",
    values_to = "count"
  )

nys_violence_2024 <- nys_violence_2024 %>%
  filter(!is.na(county), !county %in% c("DOMESTIC VIOLENCE VICTIMS REPORTED IN 2024", "NON-NEW YORK CITY COUNTIES"))

nys_violence_2024 <- nys_violence_2024 %>%
  mutate(year = 2024)

nys_violence_2024 <- nys_violence_2024 %>%
  slice(1:(n() - 24))

```

```{r}
    n_coed = sum(gender_housed == "(3) Both males and females", na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Merge into your main dataset

  left_join(ccf_county_agg, by = "GEOID") %>%
  mutate(

    n_male_only = replace_na(n_male_only, 0),
    n_female_only = replace_na(n_female_only, 0),
    n_coed = replace_na(n_coed, 0),
    any_female_or_coed = as.integer(n_female_only > 0 | n_coed > 0)
  )

# Preliminary look
master_clean %>%

  filter(prison_present == 1) %>%
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# Classify each county into one group based on what CCF facilities it has
master_grouped <- master_clean %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(prison_present == 1) %>%
  mutate(
    facility_group = case_when(
      n_coed > 0 ~ "Co-ed",
      n_female_only > 0 & n_male_only == 0 ~ "Female only",
      n_male_only > 0 & n_female_only == 0 ~ "Male only",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(facility_group))

table(master_grouped$facility_group)

# Variables to compare
vars_to_test <- c("divorce_rate", "overdose_rate", "suicide_rate", "homicide_rate",
                   "unemp_rate", "pct_poverty", "life_exp_weighted", "homeown_rate")

# Run ANOVA for each variable, plus group means
results <- lapply(vars_to_test, function(v) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste(v, "~ facility_group"))
  aov_result <- aov(formula, data = master_grouped)
  p_val <- summary(aov_result)[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1]
  
  means <- master_grouped %>%
    group_by(facility_group) %>%
    summarise(mean = mean(.data[[v]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  
  tibble(
    variable = v,
    mean_male = means$mean[means$facility_group == "Male only"],
    mean_female = means$mean[means$facility_group == "Female only"],
    mean_coed = means$mean[means$facility_group == "Co-ed"],
    p_value = p_val
  )
}) %>% bind_rows()

results %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    variable = "Variable",
    mean_male = "Male Only",
    mean_female = "Female Only",
    mean_coed = "Co-ed",
    p_value = "p-value"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(mean_male, mean_female, mean_coed), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = p_value, decimals = 4) %>%
  tab_header(title = "County Outcomes by Facility Gender Composition") %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = p_value < 0.05)
  )
```

```{r}
library(tidycensus)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(MatchIt)

treated_final <- county_prison_status %>%
  filter(treatment_group == "treated", closure_year >= 2010)

pre_years_needed <- sort(unique(treated_final$closure_year - 1))

matching_vars <- c(
  tot_pop = "B01003_001",
  medhhinc = "B25119_001",
  pop_poverty = "B17001_002",
  pop_total_poverty_universe = "B17001_001"
)

acs_by_year <- map_dfr(pre_years_needed, function(yr) {
  get_acs(geography = "county", variables = matching_vars, year = yr, survey = "acs5") %>%
    select(GEOID, variable, estimate) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) %>%
    mutate(
      log_pop = log(tot_pop),
      pct_poverty = pop_poverty / pop_total_poverty_universe,
      pre_year = yr
    )
})

run_matching_for_year <- function(target_year) {
  treated_this_year <- treated_final %>% filter(closure_year - 1 == target_year)

  cohort_data <- bind_rows(
    treated_this_year %>% mutate(treat = 1),
    county_prison_status %>% filter(treatment_group == "control_pool") %>% mutate(treat = 0)
  ) %>%
    left_join(acs_by_year %>% filter(pre_year == target_year), by = c("COUNTYFIPS" = "GEOID")) %>%
    left_join(rural_2013_clean %>% select(GEOID, RUCC_2013), by = c("COUNTYFIPS" = "GEOID")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(log_pop), !is.na(medhhinc), !is.na(pct_poverty), !is.na(RUCC_2013))

  m <- matchit(treat ~ log_pop + medhhinc + pct_poverty + RUCC_2013,
               data = cohort_data, method = "nearest", distance = "glm", ratio = 3)

  match.data(m) %>% mutate(cohort_year = target_year)
}

matched_all <- map_dfr(pre_years_needed, run_matching_for_year)

nrow(matched_all)
table(matched_all$treat)
```

```{r}
})

nrow(econ_panel_raw)

# Attach treatment info and compute event time
event_panel <- econ_panel_raw %>%
  left_join(
    matched_all %>% select(COUNTYFIPS, treat, cohort_year, subclass) %>% distinct(),
    by = c("GEOID" = "COUNTYFIPS")
  ) %>%
  mutate(years_since_closure = year - cohort_year)

table(event_panel$years_since_closure)
```

```{r}
install.packages("fixest")
library(fixest)

event_panel_reg <- event_panel %>%
  filter(years_since_closure >= -5, years_since_closure <= 5) %>%   # trim to a reasonable symmetric window
  mutate(years_since_closure = relevel(factor(years_since_closure), ref = "-1"))  # -1 is the reference period

model_income <- feols(
  medhhinc ~ treat * years_since_closure | GEOID + year,
  data = event_panel_reg,
  cluster = ~GEOID
)

summary(model_income)

model_poverty <- feols(
  pct_poverty ~ treat * years_since_closure | GEOID + year,
  data = event_panel_reg,
  cluster = ~GEOID
)

summary(model_poverty)
```
